# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 12
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 12

---

*[Hell-Tour concludes: final categories of the damned; summary statement.]*

1. And yet another region I saw near to that place. There was a great fire there, and in it were men and women whose flesh was being consumed by worms that did not die.

2. And I lamented and wept at these things, because I was very sorrowful over them.

3. And the angel said to me: "Why do you lament? Are you more compassionate than God who made all things and who determined what was right for each?"

4. And I answered the angel and said: "Yet the mercy of God — will it not prevail?"

5. And the angel said to me: "What is it that you said? God is righteous in all his ways and just in all his deeds."

6. "And to each one according to his deeds he will render recompense."

7. "The sinners shall be punished in all eternity according to the hardness of their hearts, and they shall have no rest in the fire for even a moment."

8. And I marvelled greatly at these words and said: "Righteousness and justness — who can stand before them?"

9. And the angel answered: "No one can withstand the justice of God. Only those who accepted the grace of God in their lifetime and who did the will of God shall be saved."

10. And I was troubled at the things I had heard and seen, but I glorified God the Father who gives life to all men and who judges them in righteousness.

11. Then the Lord said to me: "Let us go to the place of paradise and also to the holy mountain."

12. And we went, I and my Lord, and he rejoiced greatly in me, and I also rejoiced greatly in him.

---
*EMET note: Peter's intercession (v.4) — "will not the mercy of God prevail?" — is one of the earliest examples of the apocalyptic genre questioning the justice of eternal punishment. The angel's refusal to grant intercession is deliberate and theologically significant.*
